items.claim: The ruler-participle moshel closing Prov.29.26 is the fourth chapter-28-29 occurrence of the rule-lexeme (28:15, 29:2, 29:12, 29:26), disclosed as distinct from the melekh (king) noun at 29:4/29:14, with the shared ish token to 29:27 correctly graded skeleton-tier and rejected as cluster glue.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: מוֹשֵׁ֑ל (oshb:Prov.29.26) confirmed against source. Independent in-process resweep of the rule-root across this part (chs 28-29) returns exactly the four cited verses (28:15, 29:2, 29:12, 29:26); a naive contiguous-skeleton substring sweep for the same root also surfaces Prov.29.15's participle of a DIFFERENT root (send-away, not rule) as a contained-substring false hit -- correctly excluded by the row -- and would MISS the plene spelling at 29:26 on a defective-spelling-only sweep -- correctly included. Prov.29.4 and Prov.29.14 confirmed to open with the king noun (melekh), a distinct root, supporting the row's disambiguation. אִֽישׁ (oshb:Prov.29.26) vs צַ֭דִּיקִים (oshb:Prov.29.27) is correctly graded skeleton-tier only (the two forms carry different cantillation, not a byte-identical match) and correctly rejected as too generic for cluster weight, consistent with the atomic default.

items.claim: Prov.29.27's mutual-abomination chiasm is self-contained, closes the C5 collection, and correctly discloses the petuchah there as tier-3 corroboration rather than a boundary driver.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: צַ֭דִּיקִים (oshb:Prov.29.27) confirmed. Petuchah at Prov.29.27 confirmed present in pmarks_Prov.json (single witness, correctly labeled tier-3/non-driver, correctly not conflated with setumah -- the book's one setumah sits at Prov.24.22, outside this span). The mirrored subject/object structure (abomination-to-X repeated with terms reversed) is grammatically apt to the quoted colon. The shared ish token with the preceding verse is disclosed and rejected as cluster glue consistently with that neighboring verse's own row -- no undisclosed straddling device at this seam.

items.claim: The Agur-header unit (30:1-6) correctly discloses the massa header, the Ithiel/Ucal crux as unresolved, and the divrei sweep digits, but its device_notes misstates the book's own documented LXX crosswalk for where Lemuel's oracle relocates.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: דִּבְרֵ֤י ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (oshb:Prov.30.1), לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל (oshb:Prov.30.1), and אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו (oshb:Prov.30.6) all confirmed against source. The 19/5/2 divrei sweep digits match the book's collection-seam inventory exactly (19 total occurrences, 5 verse-initial, 2 pairing with an oracle-word as an actual header). Petuchah brackets at Prov.29.27 and Prov.30.6 confirmed in pmarks_Prov.json. The Ithiel/Ucal crux is correctly disclosed as unresolved and correctly NOT conflated with ketiv/qere -- pmarks_Prov.json's kq inventory carries no entry at Prov.30.1 (the chapter's two K/Q notes sit at 30:10 and 30:18, both outside this row's span), and the row never claims K/Q status for the crux. CHALLENGE: the toolkit's own LXX-reordering documentation states the Greek places 30:1-14 (this row's own block) after 24:22, while 30:15-33 relocates TOGETHER WITH Lemuel's oracle (31:1-9) after 24:34 -- i.e. the 24:23-34 appendix sits between the two Agur blocks in Greek order. The row's device_notes claim that 'Lemuel's oracle moves beside them too' therefore misstates the documented crosswalk: Lemuel's oracle relocates beside the LATTER half of Agur's numerical sayings, not beside this row's own 30:1-6/30:1-14 block. Non-boundary-affecting (disclosed as prose-only cross-tradition texture, never a refs entry, does not change the span or unit_type argued), but the stated 'cross-tradition fact' itself is not accurate as written.

items.claim: The two-petition unit (30:7-9) opens on a verse-initial numeral and closes on the chapter's sole YHWH-token verse, bracketed by petuchah on both ends.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: שְׁ֭תַּיִם (oshb:Prov.30.7) confirmed verse-initial, and מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה (oshb:Prov.30.9) confirmed. The '1 of 70 book-wide' digit for the exact YHWH token in ch.30 matches the book's YHWH-density inventory exactly (chapter total 1, book total 70). Petuchah brackets at Prov.30.6 and Prov.30.9 confirmed in pmarks_Prov.json, correctly disclosed single-witness/non-driver.

items.claim: Four consecutive verses (30:11-14) open on the identical dor token, an anaphoric construction-run closing on the sword-sense (not dry-morsel) homograph of the teeth-image in 30:14.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: the opening token (e.g. דּ֭וֹר, oshb:Prov.30.11) confirmed verse-initial at all four cited verses directly from each verse's own source text (not merely present somewhere in the row's citation window). Independent book-wide consonantal resweep of the same root returns exactly 5 verses total: the four cited plus one unrelated instance in the 'generation to generation' idiom elsewhere in the book -- itself a K/Q verse, not verse-initial there, and never implicated by this row's own (correctly scoped) claim. חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ (oshb:Prov.30.14) confirmed byte-tier and correctly classed as the sword-sense homograph (teeth like swords) against the book's own hazard catalog, which lists 30:14 as sword-class distinct from the unrelated dry-morsel homograph argued elsewhere at Prov.17.1. Petuchah at Prov.30.14 confirmed closing the run in pmarks_Prov.json.

items.claim: The leech's two-daughters image pivots into the chapter's first three/four numerical formula, whose four items are completed across 30:15-16 with no petuchah splitting the pair.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ (oshb:Prov.30.15) and הַ֥ב ... תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה (oshb:Prov.30.15) both confirmed against source. The four listed appetites (Sheol / the barren womb / the earth / fire) match Prov.30.16's four cola one-for-one. Petuchah at Prov.30.14 confirmed opening the unit; pmarks_Prov.json carries no petuchah entry at either Prov.30.15 or Prov.30.16, confirming the row's own claim that the mark layer is silent across its own two verses.

items.claim: The chapter's second three/four formula (30:18) carries an inline ketiv/qere pair correctly disclosed, and its fourth listed item is picked up by a five-fold derekh catchword chain closing at 30:20.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה ... וארבע (oshb:Prov.30.18) and כֵּ֤ן דֶּ֥רֶךְ (oshb:Prov.30.20) confirmed. The inline ketiv מִמֶּ֑נִּי / qere וארבע pair at Prov.30.18 confirmed byte-for-byte against source (the ketiv is correctly labeled unpointed, the qere correctly labeled pointed); pmarks_Prov.json's ketiv/qere inventory confirms exactly one K/Q note at Prov.30.18, matching. The derekh catchword count (opening all four list items of Prov.30.19, reused a fifth time at the head of Prov.30.20) is confirmed directly from source text. Petuchah brackets at Prov.30.17 and Prov.30.20 confirmed.

items.claim: The chapter's third three/four formula (30:21) is completed by two named items per verse across 30:22-23, bracketed by petuchah on both ends.
items.evidence: Byte-tier: שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ ... וְתַ֥חַת (oshb:Prov.30.21) confirmed. The four named items (a servant becoming king and a fool filled with food in Prov.30.22; an unloved woman married and a maidservant supplanting her mistress in Prov.30.23) confirmed against source, two per verse as claimed. Petuchah brackets at Prov.30.20 and Prov.30.23 confirmed in pmarks_Prov.json.
